name: Petoi Bittle X
description: A palm-sized, 9-servo quadruped dog kit from Petoi, and the direct successor to the original Kickstarter-funded Bittle — same no-solder DIY build, upgraded to an ESP32-based "Biboard" controller with on-device voice control and native Raspberry Pi mounting. Runs Petoi's open-source OpenCat firmware, the same framework behind Petoi's cat-shaped Nybble Q and its newer, cheaper Quaddle line already in this catalog.

specs.label: Battery
specs.note: ~1 hour runtime, ~1.5 hour charge via USB

specs.label: Weight
specs.note: assembled; varies by P1S alloy vs. P1L lite servos — petoi.com official specs

specs.label: Sensors
specs.note: MPU6050 or ICM42670; no camera included by default

specs.label: Controller
specs.note: 520K SRAM, 16MB flash, Wi-Fi + Bluetooth built in

specs.label: Joints
specs.note: 2 per leg + 1 neck; coreless "P1S" alloy or "P1L" lite

specs.label: Voice Control
specs.note: on-device, no cloud dependency claimed; +10 custom

specs.label: Expansion
specs.note: camera/AI vision needs a separate module or user Raspberry Pi

specs.label: Assembly
specs.note: pre-assembled option sold at a premium

sourcing: Verified against Petoi's official Bittle X and original Bittle product/spec pages, its Quaddle and Nybble Q pages, its "About" and Kickstarter history pages, and its Research Spotlight page (self-reported, treated as a starting point); the PetoiCamp/OpenCat and OpenCatEsp32-Quadruped-Robot GitHub repositories and their license files; independent reviews from Tom's Hardware, BBC Science Focus, and The Gadgeteer; Hackster.io community projects for vision/ROS/voice add-ons; an independently published paper ("OpenMutt," SAGE 2025); and Petoi's own community forum threads on servo issues. Flagged as uncertain: the exact current bundling of mechanical CAD/STL files relative to the firmware repos (present but less centralized than the software); and whether Petoi's self-reported list of research institutions using Bittle has been independently verified beyond the company's own page.

pricing.summary: Bittle X sells for $319 direct from Petoi in its base construction-kit configuration with lite plastic servos; alloy-servo and pre-assembled variants cost more. The separate AI Vision Module and robotic-arm attachment are priced and sold independently, so they aren't included in that base price.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Bittle X's firmware is genuinely open source under the MIT license (~5,300 GitHub stars), though its mechanical CAD/STL files have historically been distributed somewhat separately from the firmware repos rather than bundled into one unified open-hardware package.
